newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger says National well-placed to lead NZ govt.
newsitem.headline: Bolger says National well-placed to lead NZ govt.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said his conservative National Party was well-positioned to lead a minority government after Saturday's election but it would be a "demanding challenge".
Bolger said he had been in a similar position previously in the last election in 1993 when there had been a hung parliament on election night.
"I then worked with others to form a government that gave stable government right through despite new parties forming, old allegiances collapsing and so on," he said.
Bolger advised financial markets to behave calmly.
"I would say to the markets 'play it calm, play it long', because I am certain New Zealand will end up with stable government."
Labour leader Helen Clark said markets were aware that a government led by Labour would be responsible.

"We stand for sound economic management. We know the importance of sound business confidence and investor confidence in our economy and we will do everything we can to ensure that this country retains that confidence," she said.
